key: And they said unto him: ‘Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways; now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.’
s: With Samuel old and his sons taking bribes, the elders come to Ramah; Radak, on 8:5, takes the wrong not as wanting a king, itself commanded, but as asking in complaint, with little trust in God, who fights for those who keep His way.

evidence.gloss: If so [the king being one of the three commandments given on entering the land], why was the thing evil in the eyes of the LORD? Because they asked it in complaint and not for the sake of the commandment. Had they asked for a king to judge them in uprightness, or for Samuel to judge them all his life, or for a king chosen by his counsel to keep them in the way of the LORD, it would have been good; but saying make us a king was evil and little trust in God, and like all the nations: they had no need to be like the nations if they kept the way of the LORD, for He fights their battles.

Read the packet on 8:5 (Rashi nothing; Metzudat David brief glosses) and Radak and Metzudat David on 8:6, 8:7 and 8:20. Radak on 8:5 opens with the rabbis’ teaching that appointing a king is one of three commandments on entering the land, then explains the evil as asking in complaint, not for the commandment, and as little trust in God, who fights their battles if they keep His way; he adopts this reading in his own commentary and then records the sages’ dispute, which the sentence does not contradict.
